name: Q-Ball
caption: A brash, self-declared “Main Event,” who turned on his own Pain Incorporated stable to challenge for and win the TWL World Heavyweight Championship, then vacated it and left the promotion.

tenures.source: Billed a founding-era Pain Incorporated member who broke from the stable to challenge Billy Joe McCallister for the TWL World Heavyweight Championship at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view, winning the title; a later broadcast recaps him dropping the belt to the mat, vacating it, and quitting the promotion.

name: Billy Joe McCallister
caption: A three-time TWL World Heavyweight Champion whose reign ended when his former Pain Incorporated partner Q-Ball turned on him and took the title.

tenures.source: Billed a three-time TWL World Heavyweight Champion entering the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view, where he lost the title to his former partner Q-Ball.

name: Palimetius the Historian
caption: The TWL Intercontinental Champion since winning a ladder-and-cage match at the promotion's own Helloween event, until a challenger's ladder spot cost him the title.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning TWL Intercontinental Champion, having won the title at the promotion's own Helloween event by catching a dropped ladder belt; lost the title to Sandman at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the museum; nothing links the two.

name: Sandman
caption: A challenger billed “the People's Champ,” who dethroned the Intercontinental Champion at the promotion's own first 1999 pay-per-view before losing the title himself several months later.

tenures.source: Won the TWL Intercontinental Championship from Palimetius the Historian at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; a later broadcast records him losing the title to XeRo at the promotion's own Armageddon event.

identity.note: Several persona of the same name are recorded elsewhere in the museum under other wings; nothing links this one to any of them.

name: XeRo
caption: A self-declared lunatic billed half of a Tag Team Championship pairing whose failure to defend cost the belts, before he won the vacant Intercontinental Championship in his own right at Armageddon.

tenures.source: Billed one half of the reigning TWL World Tag Team Champions entering the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; his co-champion's no-show at that event led the promotion's own president to strip and vacate the titles after having XeRo assaulted and suspended. A later broadcast records him winning the Intercontinental Championship from Sandman at the promotion's own Armageddon event.

identity.note: Several personas of the same name are recorded elsewhere in the museum under other wings; nothing links this one to any of them.

name: Torture
caption: Half of a TWL World Tag Team Championship pairing whose failure to appear for a title defense cost his team the belts.

tenures.source: Billed one half of the reigning TWL World Tag Team Champions; failed to appear for the pairing's own scheduled title defense at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view, after which the promotion's own president declared the titles vacant.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the museum under another wing; nothing links the two.

name: Chuckie Martinez
caption: A brash, self-billed “Latino Lust Machine” who retained the TWL Cruiserweight Championship at the promotion's own first 1999 pay-per-view before losing it, then spent the rest of the surviving record chasing it back.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning TWL Cruiserweight Champion entering the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view, retaining the title there under the promotion's own no-title-change-on-count-out rule; a later broadcast records him having since lost the title, and he appears as a non-title challenger for it on the promotion's own 3 May 1999 broadcast.

name: “The Brutal Enforcer” X
caption: A towering challenger recruited to strip the Cruiserweight Champion of his title on a technicality, who won the bout by count-out but left empty-handed under the promotion's own title rules.

tenures.source: Recruited by a rival wrestler to exploit a loophole in the TWL Cruiserweight division's own weight rule, challenging for the title at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; won the bout by count-out, but the title could not change hands on that finish.

identity.note: Several personas of the same one-letter ring name are recorded elsewhere in the museum under other wings; nothing links this one to any of them.

name: Adrian Blades
caption: A self-proclaimed “greatest TWL Television Champion of all time,” billed the belt's longest-reigning holder, who was cheated out of the title in a multi-man conspiracy at Armageddon.

tenures.source: Billed the longest-reigning TWL Television Champion, retaining the title against Exodus at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view and against Prince Geatar on its own 21 February 1999 broadcast; a later broadcast records him losing the title to Dave Davidson in a multi-man conspiracy at the promotion's own Armageddon event, after which he pursued the vacant World Heavyweight Championship.

name: Exodus
caption: A hard-hitting newcomer who fell just short of the Television Championship at the promotion's own first 1999 pay-per-view after his own allies' interference backfired.

tenures.source: Earned a TWL Television Championship shot by winning a five-way qualifier on the promotion's own 4 January 1999 broadcast, then challenged for the title at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view, coming up just short after interference from the champion's own allies.

identity.note: Several personas of the same name are recorded elsewhere in the museum under other wings; nothing links this one to any of them.

name: Prince Geatar
caption: A tag-team veteran who fell short in a Television Championship challenge, and whose past reign with the title is recalled in the promotion's own broadcasts.

tenures.source: Recorded as a past TWL Television Champion in the promotion's own broadcast flashbacks; challenged unsuccessfully for the title held by Adrian Blades on the promotion's own 21 February 1999 broadcast.

name: Anthony Levert
caption: A singles standout who captured the Cruiserweight Championship after his old tag team broke up, then lost it in a screwjob at Armageddon at the hands of his own rival.

tenures.source: Billed a past TWL Cruiserweight Champion, having won the title after his tag team Objects of Your Desire broke up; a later broadcast records him being cheated out of the title by Devon Case's interference at the promotion's own Armageddon event, and he appeared as a non-title challenger for the belt on the promotion's own 3 May 1999 broadcast.

name: El Puerco
caption: A masked luchador billed the TWL Cruiserweight Champion after winning the title in a widely questioned finish at Armageddon.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning TWL Cruiserweight Champion, having won the title at the promotion's own Armageddon event in a finish its own broadcast team called questionable; retained the title in a non-title four-corners bout ruled a no-contest on the promotion's own 3 May 1999 broadcast.

name: Devon Case
caption: A cocky rival whose interference cost Anthony Levert the Cruiserweight Championship at Armageddon.

tenures.source: Billed as costing Anthony Levert the TWL Cruiserweight Championship through interference at the promotion's own Armageddon event; competed in a non-title four-corners bout for the belt on the promotion's own 3 May 1999 broadcast.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is recorded elsewhere in the museum under another wing, in the same year; nothing beyond the shared name links the two.
Shares a bare ring name with 6 held records; no card, operator, roster or text ties this post's character to any of them, so they are filed distinct.

name: “Delicious” Dave Davidson
caption: A cocky newcomer who cheated Adrian Blades out of the Television Championship in a multi-man conspiracy at Armageddon.

tenures.source: Debuted as a TWL newcomer on the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; a later broadcast records him taking the Television Championship from Adrian Blades through a multi-man conspiracy at the promotion's own Armageddon event.

name: “Simply Irresistible” Jeff Jacob
caption: One half of the tag team Sex Sells, who won the TWL World Tag Team Championship in a ladder match after the belts were vacated.

tenures.source: One half of the tag team Sex Sells; won the TWL World Tag Team Championship with his partner in a title-deciding ladder match on the promotion's own 21 February 1999 broadcast.

name: “Dollar Man” Matthew Hutchinson
caption: One half of the tag team Sex Sells, who won the TWL World Tag Team Championship in a ladder match after the belts were vacated.

tenures.source: One half of the tag team Sex Sells; won the TWL World Tag Team Championship with his partner in a title-deciding ladder match on the promotion's own 21 February 1999 broadcast.

name: Bill Collins
caption: The promotion's own on-screen president, whose ruling stripped and vacated the World Tag Team Championship after one of its two champions failed to appear.

tenures.source: Billed the TWL's own on-screen president; declared the World Tag Team Championship vacant at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view after one champion no-showed and had the other assaulted and suspended, then ordered a title-deciding match for the promotion's own 21 February 1999 broadcast.

name: "Blitz Lightning" Matt Kreig
notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (10 May 1999), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/rp-blitz-lightning-matt-kreig-please-critique-1999-05-10.html; his appearance (a pale, white-blond, gymnast-built cruiserweight in a white cape with blue lightning bolts) is described in his 23 April 1999 intro roleplay, served live at /promotions/twl-1998/archive/twl-1998-flash-forward-1999-05-01.html
caption: A pale, gymnast-built TWL cruiserweight whose motto is that lightning strikes twice, April to May 1999.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/rp-blitz-lightning-matt-kreig-please-critique-1999-05-10.html

name: Maurice Martin
notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (12 May 1999), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/rolepay-maurice-martin-critique-please-1999-05-12.html: Maurice Martin, the 'Madling Maniac', walks into a burned Harlem warehouse, speaks of his father and sister and promises Alex Cote a massacre on Monday Night at the Tough Wrestling League.
caption: The 'Madling Maniac', a new Tough Wrestling League wrestler in a Harlem warehouse promo of 12 May 1999.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/rolepay-maurice-martin-critique-please-1999-05-12.html
